findings.problem: opts.nowMs is never validated, unlike its sibling opts.frameByteLength which IS strictly validated at wire.ts:27-29. Passing nowMs as undefined or NaN makes both expiry comparisons (expiresAt <= nowMs and expiresAt > nowMs + maxRequestTtlMs) evaluate to false, so the request is accepted. Same defect in delivery.ts:63 for notAfter.
findings.impact: The bounded-expiry guarantee that AC3 requires, and that architecture.md advertises as 'request expiresAt (now, now+60s]', is silently and completely disabled by a caller-side mistake rather than failing closed. Verified empirically: validateWireRequest(validReq, {nowMs: undefined, frameByteLength: 100}) and {nowMs: NaN, ...} both return ok:true with an arbitrary expiresAt. Not exploitable in S0 (no live callers exist yet), but this is the exact trust-boundary guarantee the package is built to provide, and the asymmetry with frameByteLength shows it is an oversight rather than a documented contract.
findings.requiredFix: Validate nowMs with the same strictness already applied to frameByteLength: reject with a stable 'malformed' error unless Number.isInteger(opts.nowMs) (or at minimum Number.isFinite). Apply in validateWireRequest and validateStaticDelivery. Add negative tests for nowMs undefined/NaN/non-number.

findings.problem: validateOnceSchedule validates atUtc with a shape-only regex (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T...) and then only checks Number.isFinite(Date.parse(...)). It never round-trips the parse, so calendar dates that do not exist are accepted and silently roll over to a different day.
findings.impact: Verified: '2026-02-30T00:00:00Z' is accepted and resolves to 2026-03-02; '2026-04-31T00:00:00Z' is accepted and resolves to 2026-05-01. For a message-scheduling protocol this means a malformed schedule is admitted at the trust boundary and will later fire on a date the requester never asked for, with no error surfaced anywhere. AC3 requires rejecting malformed input; the spec-conformance reviewer should weigh this against AC3 explicitly. (Note: '2026-09-21T24:00:00Z' -> 2026-09-22T00:00 is legitimate ISO-8601 end-of-day and is not part of this finding. Out-of-range month/second values such as month 13, month 00 and second 60 ARE correctly rejected.)
findings.requiredFix: After Date.parse, round-trip verify: reject unless new Date(ms).toISOString() matches the input normalized for the optional .SSS fraction. Add negative tests for 2026-02-30 and 2026-04-31.

findings.problem: isPlainObject accepts any non-null non-array object and all field reads use dot access, which traverses the prototype chain. No Object.hasOwn guard is applied anywhere in wire.ts, delivery.ts, jobs.ts or adapter.ts.
findings.impact: If any other code in the host process pollutes Object.prototype, these validators will happily synthesize valid objects out of inherited properties. Verified: with Object.prototype.{profileId,adapterId,accountId,chatId,threadId} set, validateDeliveryRoute({}) returns ok:true with a fully attacker-controlled route; likewise validateWireRequest({}) returns ok:true. The package does not itself cause pollution - I confirmed JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{...}}') creates an own property and leaves Object.prototype clean - so this is a defense-in-depth gap in a component whose stated job is trust-boundary validation, not a standalone vulnerability.
findings.requiredFix: Guard reads with Object.hasOwn(obj, key), or have isPlainObject additionally require Object.getPrototypeOf(value) === Object.prototype || null.

findings.problem: LIMITS, METHODS, KNOWN_CAPABILITIES and RECEIPT_LEVELS are exported with 'as const', which is a compile-time-only annotation. None are Object.freeze'd, so they are mutable shared module state for every consumer of a given module root.
findings.impact: Verified: setting LIMITS.maxTextChars = 1 at runtime caused a previously valid delivery to be rejected with text_too_long, i.e. one consumer can silently change validation semantics for every other consumer in the same module instance. This sits uneasily with the 'stateless' claim in packages/protocol/README.md:5 and architecture.md:11. It does NOT violate the literal 'no runtime singleton / no class/Symbol identity' claim, which G5 independently confirms. Defense in depth noted: mutating METHODS to add an unknown method still failed closed, because validateMethodBody's switch default (jobs.ts:100-101) rejects anything without an explicit case.
findings.requiredFix: Object.freeze the exported constant objects and arrays in limits.ts. Low urgency; no untrusted-input path reaches this in S0.

findings.problem: validateWireRequest declares a total ProtocolResult return type but can throw. Reading input.body triggers a getter; if that getter throws, the exception propagates out of the validator instead of being converted to a stable error.
findings.impact: Verified: an input object with a throwing 'body' getter escapes as a raw Error. The JSON.stringify path is correctly guarded by try/catch at wire.ts:57-61 (BigInt, circular references and a throwing toJSON all return a clean invalid_body), so this is only reachable with non-JSON-derived inputs. Real callers parse JSON, which cannot produce getters, so impact is confined to in-process misuse.
findings.requiredFix: Either document that input must be JSON-derived, or wrap property access in the existing try/catch so the function is total as typed.

findings.problem: validateJobCreate explicitly discards the clock with 'void nowMs', so a 'once' schedule carries no temporal bound at all. Verified: atUtc of 1999-01-01 and of 9999-01-01 are both accepted.
findings.impact: Unbounded-in-both-directions job schedules pass the trust boundary. This is arguably a deliberate S0 deferral, since the contract forbids implementing scheduling in this lane and the catch-up/anchoring policy is genuinely an S1 decision. However architecture.md's 'Open items deferred' list records only the related-but-different question of notAfter anchoring for job-created deliveries; the absence of any bound on atUtc itself is not recorded anywhere. Flagged for the spec/AC reviewer rather than treated as a code-safety defect.
findings.requiredFix: Either bound atUtc (e.g. must be > nowMs) or add an explicit line to the deferred-items list in docs/architecture.md stating that atUtc temporal bounds are deferred to S1. Documentation-truthfulness item, not a code-safety blocker.

verifiedClean: No hidden Pi/transport/global dependency: compiled dist contains zero non-relative imports and zero occurrences of node:*, process.*, globalThis, __dirname, eval( or Function(. package-lock.json holds exactly one external package (typescript@5.9.3, devDependency).
No import side effects: importing dist/index.js changed globalThis key count by 0, process.env key count by 0 and process listener count by 0. sideEffects:false is truthful.
No install behavior: zero preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare/prepublish*/prepack/postpack scripts in either manifest; zero lockfile entries with hasInstallScript.
No secrets, credentials, network, filesystem or child-process use anywhere in packages/protocol/src.
utf8ByteLength is exactly correct: matched Buffer.byteLength on all 8 probes including lone surrogates (\uD800, \uDFFF), an unpaired high surrogate followed by ASCII, NUL and a 4-byte emoji.

No unvalidated passthrough or aliasing: validated output is always a freshly constructed object. Unknown keys are stripped at both top level and nested route level, and the returned value never aliases the attacker-supplied object (verified explicitly).
Malformed-JSON robustness: BigInt bodies, circular references and throwing toJSON all yield a stable invalid_body rather than a crash. Arrays, null and non-objects are rejected as malformed.

Numeric edge cases handled: expiresAt of NaN, Infinity, 1e21, -0 and string forms are all rejected; frameByteLength of undefined, null, '200', 1.5, {} and a missing key are all rejected as malformed; 65536 accepted and 65537 rejected at the exact boundary.
No ReDoS: all patterns are flat bounded character classes. A 1MB requestId was rejected in 0.41ms; a 1MB timeZone was rejected in 19ms.

Adapter manifest negatives all correct (12/12): duplicate capability, unknown capability, empty capabilities, array-like non-array capabilities, apiVersion 2/1.5/'1', maxTextLength 0 and 99999, receiptLevels missing 'accepted', duplicate receiptLevel, configSchemaVersion 0.
Clean packed consumer: tarball ships only dist + README (34 files, 0 src/, 0 test/, 0 tsconfig), installs and imports by package name in a fresh temp consumer with no ambient Pi or transport module.
Independent module roots: two separate copies yield distinct namespaces and distinct function references with structurally identical results - no singleton identity requirement.

Documentation truthfulness spot-checked: architecture.md's concrete limits table matches limits.ts exactly; the 'max text = UTF-16 code units' wording matches the actual .length check; toolchain versions (Node v24.20.0, npm 11.19.0, tsc 5.9.3) match what I observed; provenance.md's 'runtime dependencies: none' and 'no lifecycle scripts' claims are both true; no LICENSE file and no license field, consistent with the stated deliberate deferral.
unverified: Any live transport, network, model, Telegram or WhatsApp operation - S0 ships no transport; OUT OF SCOPE for this stage and explicitly NOT marked PASS.
Node/SQLite behaviour on Node versions other than the observed v24.20.0 / sqlite 3.53.4.
systemd user-unit linger and logout survival.
Pi CLI isolation flags and provider credential behaviour under a user unit.
npm scope ownership, publication identity and outbound license choice.
notAfter anchoring for job-created deliveries (S1 decision, correctly deferred in docs).

G4's clean-consumer install runs npm install with --ignore-scripts; behaviour without that flag was not exercised. Indirect evidence that there is no script surface: the lockfile has zero hasInstallScript entries and the package declares zero dependencies.
Coverage is measured against compiled dist rather than TypeScript sources, so the 88.05%/78.98% figures are dist-line-based.
Spec compliance, origin/AC conformance and observable S0 outcome - deliberately NOT judged here; these are separate reviewer stages.
